The searches are placeholders until the owner picks specific products; swap "search" for "asin" to link one. "keys" match the shopping list in the report (trebgen.hardware.bill_of_materials).

starterKit.title: Hardware kit for the desk trebuchet
starterKit.intro: Besides the printed parts, this is everything the default trebuchet needs. Most come in packs, so you'll have spares for a second build.

items.why: Two press into the frames: the smoothest axle you can get, so more throw.
The main axle. Check the length in your shopping list.
The hinge bolt for the counterweight bucket, plus nuts and washers.
Hold the frames, cross members and trough together.
The sling cords: strong and doesn't stretch.
A small piece makes the sling pouch.
The release ring that slides off the pin.

categories.title: Axle and hinge hardware
categories.intro: The arm swings on an M8 bolt through two 608 skateboard bearings; the counterweight hangs on an M4 bolt. Lock nuts (nylon insert) stop them shaking loose.

items.name: 608 bearings (8 × 22 × 7 mm)
items.note: Skateboard size. Get the sealed (2RS) kind; you need two.

items.search: M8 hex bolts nylon lock nuts washers kit
items.name: M8 bolts, lock nuts and washers
items.note: The axle. The report says how long (90 mm for the default design); longer is fine with a washer stack.

items.search: M4 bolt nut washer assortment kit
items.name: M4 bolt, nut and washer kit
items.note: For the bucket hinge. A kit covers the lengths for every size the designer makes.

items.search: M3 self tapping screws assortment for plastic
items.name: M3 self-tapping screws for plastic
items.note: 10 per trebuchet. #4 × 1/2" sheet-metal screws work too.

categories.title: Sling, release and trigger
categories.intro: The sling is two cords and a pouch; a ring on one cord slides off the release pin to let go. A cord loop and pin hold the arm down until you fire.

items.name: Braided fishing line, 20 lb or more
items.note: Thin, strong and barely stretches, so the release is repeatable.

items.name: Nylon twine or kite string
items.note: For the trigger loop. Any strong string works.

items.name: Leather craft scraps
items.note: Cut a 30 × 50 mm pouch and punch a hole at each end. Felt or denim also works.

items.name: Small split rings (10–12 mm)
items.note: The release ring. A tied loop works too, but a ring slides off more cleanly.

items.name: Large paper clips
items.note: Straighten one for the release pin (about 2 mm thick), or use a small nail.

categories.title: Counterweight fill
categories.intro: The heavier the fill for its size, the smaller the bucket. Weigh it on a kitchen scale.

items.name: Steel BBs (4.5 mm)
items.note: Densest easy fill, and they pour. About 350 g fills the default bucket.

items.name: Steel nuts, bulk
items.note: A box of nuts makes a tidy, reusable counterweight.

items.name: Play sand
items.note: Cheap but light, so the bucket comes out bigger.

items.name: Digital kitchen scale
items.note: To weigh the fill and your projectiles: the estimate is only as good as the numbers.

categories.title: Things to throw
categories.intro: Light and round goes farthest. The kit includes a printable ball; these are the other choices in the designer.

items.name: Small foam balls
items.note: Safe indoors.

items.name: Ping-pong balls
items.note: Light and big: they slow down fast in the air. Fun indoors.

items.name: Glass marbles (16 mm)
items.note: Heavy and fast. Outdoors only, with a clear field.

items.name: Mini marshmallows
items.note: The classic desk-trebuchet ammo.

categories.title: Filament
categories.intro: What I print with. The whole default trebuchet takes about 220 g. Sunlu, 1.75 mm, 1 kg spools; other colours are on each listing.

items.name: Sunlu PLA, 1 kg
items.note: Easiest to print and stiff: right for the frames and trough.

items.name: Sunlu PLA+ 2.0, 1 kg
items.note: Tougher PLA. Good for the arm, which takes the most force.

items.name: Sunlu PETG, 1 kg
items.note: Tougher still and less brittle, if your arm or bucket ears crack.

categories.title: Safety and testing
categories.intro: Glasses for the throw, and a tape to measure it: compare your throws with the estimate.

items.name: Safety glasses
items.note: Impact-rated, for everyone near the throw.

items.name: Long measuring tape
items.note: Measure from the axle to where it lands. Try five throws and take the middle one.

items.name: Screwdriver and spanner set
items.note: For the M3 screws and the lock nuts.
